subject: brrrr math when refi fails
preheader: the moment a brrrr stops being a brrrr.
headline: A BRRRR screen needs an appraisal and refinance downside case.
body: BRRRR is Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat. The strategy's capital-recovery result depends on the appraised value, eligible value basis, program LTV, seasoning, coverage, credit, reserves, property, and lender approval—not ARV alone.
A useful scenario is refinance proceeds = entered ARV × an assumed LTV, compared with all-in cash. Treat the LTV as an input to verify with a lender; there is no universal 70-75% cash-out limit.

Illustration only: buy at $200,000, enter $40,000 rehab and $10,000 closing and holding, for $250,000 all-in. At an assumed $310,000 appraisal and 75% LTV, modeled gross proceeds are $232,500 before refinance costs and lender adjustments, leaving at least $17,500 in the deal.

Stress both ARV and rehab, then also test lower eligible proceeds, longer timing, refinance costs, and the stabilized payment. Meeting a modeled threshold does not guarantee an appraisal or loan approval.
